Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a compact traceability map and an example manifest. High-level answers up front, and I'll loop in Ops for the export options and signed artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Event types: we log authentication events (login, mfa_fail/mfa_success), token issuance/rotation, API calls (admin/console), role/permission changes, service-account lifecycle, model-deployment actions (deploy/rollback), dataset access requests, key-management events, and operator-runbook changes. Full list attached.
- Retention: default 365 days for admin events (configurable to 90/180/365/730 on Dedicated/Private plans); hosted customers can request legal hold snapshots for longer retention.
- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) is our default export for fidelity; we also support Parquet for analytics-ready extracts and CSV for small samples. Exports include ISO8601 utc timestamps and a normalized event_time field.
- Delivery: presigned S3 PUT for large exports, SFTP push, Azure Blob SAS, or password-protected TLS download links. For scheduled exports we can stage to a customer bucket with lifecycle rules.
- Chain-of-custody: we can produce an export manifest (CSV) with event range, record count, SHA256 checksum per file, and a signed manifest (RSA2048) on request. PGP symmetric or RSA encrypt-before-transfer supported for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Sample: providing a 10-row NDJSON sample + manifest.

Action: Vanessa will confirm the retention options and signing workflow; Diego will attach the sample manifest and S3 presigned instructions. We'll get this to you by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
--
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Lara / Sofia,

A couple of operational clarifications from retention and signing perspective:

- Retention tiers: Hosted default = 365 days (soft delete flow + 90-day purge window), Dedicated customers may choose 730 days with a contractual T&Cs addendum, Private/on-prem customers control retention fully.
- Per-scope retention: we can scope retention by event class (e.g., auth vs operator actions) for Dedicated/Private; scoping on Hosted is limited to account-level settings.
- Export cadence & snapshots: single ad-hoc exports, scheduled daily export bundles (UTC midnight window), and certified snapshot (signed + timestamped) for audit events. Certified snapshot includes a signed manifest (manifest.csv) and a checksums file (checksums.sha256).
- Signing: we support RSA-signed manifests (SHA256withRSA). We can also provide a notarized time-stamp token (RFC3161) for certified snapshots if you need attestation of creation time.
- Redaction: PII fields are redacted by default from customer-facing extracts unless a redaction waiver is signed; we offer field-level hashing for identifiers where needed.

I attach our short traceability map and an example manifest. If Brightline's auditor wants a particular CSV schema, send the schema and we'll produce a matched sample.

Thanks,
--
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Lara — attaching the small sample bundle and instructions. Quick notes inline.

Attachments (bundled):
- audit_extract_manifest.csv  (fields: file_name,file_size_bytes,record_count,range_start,range_end,sha256_hex)
- sample_events.ndjson  (10 events, ISO8601 UTC timestamps, event_type,principal_id,resource,action,meta.*)
- s3_presigned_instructions.txt (how to accept/verify a presigned PUT, expected object keys and ACLs)
- chain_of_custody_checksums.sha256 (SHA256 hashes for each file in the bundle)

Operational checks:
- Timezone: all exported timestamps are normalized to UTC and annotated with event_time and recorded_at.
- Event IDs: every logged event includes a stable event_id (UUID v4) for cross-referencing with traces/alerts.
- Ordering: exports are sorted by event_time ascending; manifest.range_start/range_end reflect the first/last event_time.
- Verification: to verify the bundle, download files, compute local SHA256, compare to chain_of_custody file, then validate manifest signature which is available on request (we can publish the RSA public key or include a signed token).

If you want us to push the full 30-day extract to a customer S3 bucket, tell us the bucket name and preferred delivery method and we'll create a presigned PUT workflow. For immediate auditor review, the attached sample and the manifest should meet SIG evidence expectations.

Cheers,
--
Diego Fernandez
Lead, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
